top.statement: Filtering a patient by diagnosis and description date is expressed as a subquery on Patient.ID used with IN, rather than a JOIN to Patient.
A per-unit price filter is expressed as Price divided by Amount compared to the threshold, without an additional Amount > 0 guard.

Counting patients who satisfy a condition on an examination attribute requires joining Examination to the patient identifier and counting that identifier, rather than counting rows from a Patient table joined only on shared IDs.
When a question asks for a count of patients, counting rows from a single joined table pair without DISTINCT can overcount patients who have multiple matching rows in the joined table.
A query that ranks teams by count of away wins must group by the team identifier used in the join, not by the team name column.

When a question asks for the percentage of atoms of a given element among atoms in molecules matching a bond-type filter, the numerator and denominator must both count distinct atom_id values, because joining atom to bond multiplies atom rows by the number of matching bonds per molecule.
Patient-level questions join Laboratory to Patient on ID rather than querying Laboratory alone.
When a question asks to list cards, the SELECT clause projects the card identifier column rather than all columns of the cards table.
When a question asks for school names, the name must be selected from the frpm table's `School Name` column rather than from a schools table's School column.
Questions asking who achieved something in a race require selecting driver identity columns (forename, surname, url) rather than only the driver url.
A driver is counted as having finished a race only when results.time is not null.
A percentage of cards in a given language is computed over the cards table joined to foreign_data on uuid, not over foreign_data alone.
When a question asks which user performed an action on a post, the result set includes both the user's display name and the post's title.
A phrase about a player remaining in position when the team attacks maps to the attacking_work_rate column, and a phrase about preferred foot maps to the preferred_foot column.
Post popularity is measured by summing ViewCount over posts reached through postHistory rather than over posts owned directly by the user.
Text about a card's abilities is stored in the rulings table, not in the cards table.
A percentage eligible for FRPM is computed as the FRPM count divided by enrollment, multiplied by 100, rather than read from a precomputed percent column.

A percentage comparison between two named players' overall ratings requires each player's rating to be selected by matching player_name in Player and joining Player_Attributes on player_api_id, not by ordering Player_Attributes rows and taking a single LIMIT 1 row.
Patient-level questions join Laboratory to Patient on ID rather than querying Laboratory alone.
Joins between votes, posts, and users are ordered posts to votes to users, with each join keyed on the matching Id column.

best.statement: A query that asks who is the youngest among drivers who finished a race filters results to rows where the finish time is non-null.
A query that joins cards to sets and filters by set name and language must select DISTINCT to avoid duplicate rows when multiple cards match.
The Laboratory.SM column encodes normal anti-SM results as the values 'negative' and '0'.
Wrapping a percentage computation in NULLIF to guard against division by zero produces a result that does not match the expected execution.
A question asking for a metric of the top N teams returns only that metric column, not the team name column.
The phrase 'would remain in his position when the team attacked' maps to the attacking_work_rate column with value 'low'.
When a question asks for tags used in posts, the posts table's Tags column already stores the tag values, so joining a separate tags table is unnecessary.
A driver's first race is identified by ordering races by year ascending and taking the earliest, without requiring a round tiebreaker.
A query that asks for a list of entities should select only the identifying column of the primary table rather than all columns.
A city or district filter on a school-location question is applied to the district/location column of the schools or frpm table, not to a column of the satscores table.
A query that asks who is the youngest among a set of drivers selects only the identifying name columns, not the birth-date column used for ordering.
The DOC column in the schools table holds the DOC type of a school.
When a question asks for an aggregate over posts together with per-comment text, the aggregate is computed over the joined post-comment rows rather than over posts alone.
String literals compared against attribute_name must match the stored casing exactly, such as 'Durability' rather than 'durability'.
When a question asks for the top entity by a numeric attribute, the query orders by the attribute value column descending and limits to one row.
A join path from users to comments must traverse posts via posts.OwnerUserId and comments.PostId rather than joining users directly to comments on a user id.
A request for a racer's full name is satisfied by selecting forename and surname as separate columns rather than concatenating them into one column.
Counting non-distinct IDs after joining Patient to Laboratory and Examination overcounts patients who have multiple matching rows.
